title: Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — Premium Revision Paper #19

pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Plural means (1 mark)
   A. nothing
   B. the biggest
   C. only one
   D. more than one

2. In the passage: Ugali is made from maize flour, what is ugali made from? (1 mark)
   A. wheat only
   B. rice
   C. maize flour
   D. millet

3. When copying a sentence, what should you check? (1 mark)
   A. Only the page number
   B. Only the date
   C. Only the colour of the pen
   D. Letter size, spacing, capital letter and full stop

4. A sentence should end with a (1 mark)
   A. full stop
   B. drawing
   C. capital letter
   D. comma

5. A good comment during a gallery walk is (1 mark)
   A. Nothing to say
   B. Your spacing is very even
   C. You cannot write
   D. This is ugly

6. What is an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. A list of names
   B. A type of poem
   C. A story about animals
   D. Words that tell someone what to do

7. Why should instructions be clear? (1 mark)
   A. So people are confused
   B. So they are longer
   C. So nobody listens
   D. So the listener can do the right thing

8. Which way of reading a sad part is best? (1 mark)
   A. Fast and loud
   B. Slowly and softly
   C. Laughing
   D. Without pausing

9. What is wrong with: it rained all night. (1 mark)
   A. It needs no changes
   B. It needs two full stops
   C. It needs a comma after it
   D. It needs a capital letter at the start

10. What should you do if you did not hear a question? (1 mark)
   A. Politely ask for it to be repeated
   B. Leave
   C. Laugh
   D. Guess loudly

11. Which is the best first step to find the meaning of a new word in a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Read the words around it for clues
   B. Skip the whole page
   C. Ask nobody
   D. Tear the page

12. What is a word puzzle used for? (1 mark)
   A. Practising vocabulary in a fun way
   B. Cooking
   C. Running
   D. Painting

13. In The road was congested and the matatu could not move, what does congested mean? (1 mark)
   A. Very clean
   B. Very short
   C. Very wide
   D. Very crowded

14. Where do oral narratives come from? (1 mark)
   A. From machines only
   B. From elders and storytellers who pass them on
   C. From only one book
   D. From nowhere

15. What is a good rule for handling library books? (1 mark)
   A. Leave them outside
   B. Write in them
   C. Fold the corners
   D. Turn pages gently and return them on time

16. What does the Kiswahili proverb Kidole kimoja hakivunji chawa teach? (1 mark)
   A. Lice are dangerous
   B. We need to work together
   C. Never use your hands
   D. One finger is very strong

17. What is an imaginative composition? (1 mark)
   A. A list of prices
   B. A story made from the imagination
   C. A weather forecast
   D. A news report

18. Why do we check a dictionary meaning against the sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Sentences have no meaning
   B. Words can have more than one meaning
   C. Dictionaries are wrong
   D. Words never change

19. Where should the comma go in I have money and I want a book? (1 mark)
   A. Before and
   B. After I
   C. After want
   D. After have

20. What is a receipt? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of coin
   B. A paper that shows you paid
   C. A shop
   D. A type of fruit

21. Who should you call for a sick animal? (1 mark)
   A. A veterinary doctor
   B. A driver
   C. A tailor
   D. A shopkeeper

22. Which preposition needs two things to make sense? (1 mark)
   A. in
   B. under
   C. between
   D. on

23. What does it mean to advocate for animal welfare? (1 mark)
   A. To speak in support of caring for animals
   B. To harm animals
   C. To ignore them
   D. To hide them

24. What should you do while a classmate recites? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh
   B. Talk
   C. Listen and respect them
   D. Leave

25. What is the meaning of reciting a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Erasing it
   B. Writing it
   C. Copying it
   D. Saying it aloud, usually from memory

26. Which starting sentence would make a reader curious? (1 mark)
   A. The end.
   B. Page one.
   C. Yes.
   D. One cloudy afternoon, Neema saw a thin dog under a tree.

27. What is a polite way to disagree in a debate? (1 mark)
   A. I respectfully disagree
   B. Leave now
   C. You are wrong and silly
   D. Shut up

28. Which interjection fits a small mistake? (1 mark)
   A. Wow
   B. Hurray
   C. Oops
   D. Bravo

29. Which is NOT a feeling shown by interjections? (1 mark)
   A. Disgust
   B. Pain
   C. Joy
   D. The price of an item

30. In a script dialogue, what comes straight after the speaker's name? (1 mark)
   A. A number
   B. A full stop
   C. A bracket
   D. A colon

31. Which of these can begin a happy line? (1 mark)
   A. Hurray!
   B. Yuck!
   C. Oh no!
   D. Ouch!

32. What is a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. A map
   B. A list
   C. A conversation between two or more people
   D. A long description

33. Why do we match devices to their uses? (1 mark)
   A. To know what each is for
   B. To lose them
   C. To break them
   D. To hide them

34. What is a digital device? (1 mark)
   A. A type of song
   B. A wooden tool
   C. A machine that works with electronic signals to help us communicate or work
   D. A kind of fruit

35. Which adjective describes colour? (1 mark)
   A. large
   B. silver
   C. thin
   D. tall

36. What should you use to fill a form unless told otherwise? (1 mark)
   A. A finger
   B. A chalk
   C. A pen
   D. A crayon

37. Why should you ask an adult before giving your address on an online form? (1 mark)
   A. No reason
   B. To waste time
   C. To make it longer
   D. To stay safe

38. What is a talking object used for? (1 mark)
   A. To throw
   B. To show who may speak
   C. To play with
   D. To hide

39. Why is it important to obey leaders? (1 mark)
   A. It is a game
   B. It is boring
   C. It keeps order, peace and safety
   D. It makes noise

40. What is a good leader described as in the model poem? (1 mark)
   A. Rude
   B. Fair and kind
   C. Lazy
   D. Angry

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give three rules for punctuating a dialogue. (3 marks)

42. Explain two differences between an advert and a news item. (4 marks)

43. List three steps for skimming. (3 marks)

44. Explain why pace matters when reading a poem. (3 marks)

45. Write one simile and one metaphor about a teacher. (3 marks)

46. Give three rules for writing clear instructions. (3 marks)

47. Name three headings in a story plan. (3 marks)

48. Write one correct line of a dialogue with a speaker name and an interjection. (2 marks)

49. Make an instruction chart of five steps for keeping the class clean. Include a title and start each step with a verb. (5 marks)

50. Describe three rules for writing tidily on lined paper. (3 marks)

51. Describe how a newsreader should read a weather bulletin. (4 marks)

52. Add capital letters, commas and full stops: on friday we bought rice beans and flour (3 marks)

53. Describe the steps in writing a story from a picture. (4 marks)

54. Write the verbs in this instruction: Close the door and sit down. (2 marks)

55. Write the four parts of a telephone conversation and give a short example of one. (4 marks)

56. Compose a short poem of four lines about caring for animals. Make two lines rhyme. (5 marks)

57. List three steps for understanding a poem. (3 marks)

58. Explain why clear instructions are important when it rains. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #19 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — more than one
   Plural nouns name two or more.

2. C — maize flour
   The passage states that ugali is made from maize flour.

3. D — Letter size, spacing, capital letter and full stop
   These are the points of neat copying.

4. A — full stop
   A statement ends with a full stop.

5. B — Your spacing is very even
   Kind and specific comments help writers.

6. D — Words that tell someone what to do
   An instruction says what to do.

7. D — So the listener can do the right thing
   Clear instructions prevent mistakes.

8. B — Slowly and softly
   A slow, soft voice matches sadness.

9. D — It needs a capital letter at the start
   The first word of a sentence must begin with a capital letter.

10. A — Politely ask for it to be repeated
   Asking politely helps you answer correctly.

11. A — Read the words around it for clues
   Context clues are the words nearby.

12. A — Practising vocabulary in a fun way
   Puzzles help pupils remember words.

13. D — Very crowded
   The matatu could not move because there was too much traffic.

14. B — From elders and storytellers who pass them on
   They are passed on by word of mouth.

15. D — Turn pages gently and return them on time
   Good care keeps books usable for others.

16. B — We need to work together
   One finger cannot crush a louse, so cooperation is needed.

17. B — A story made from the imagination
   Imaginative compositions are made-up stories.

18. B — Words can have more than one meaning
   The right meaning depends on context.

19. A — Before and
   A comma comes before the joining word.

20. B — A paper that shows you paid
   A receipt is proof of payment.

21. A — A veterinary doctor
   Veterinary doctors treat animals.

22. C — between
   Between means with something on each side.

23. A — To speak in support of caring for animals
   Advocating means speaking in support.

24. C — Listen and respect them
   Good listeners respect performers.

25. D — Saying it aloud, usually from memory
   To recite is to say aloud.

26. D — One cloudy afternoon, Neema saw a thin dog under a tree.
   A specific opening makes the reader want to read on.

27. A — I respectfully disagree
   Polite words show respect.

28. C — Oops
   Oops shows a small mistake.

29. D — The price of an item
   Interjections show feelings, not prices.

30. D — A colon
   The name is followed by a colon.

31. A — Hurray!
   Hurray shows happiness.

32. C — A conversation between two or more people
   A dialogue is people talking.

33. A — To know what each is for
   Knowing the use helps us choose the right device.

34. C — A machine that works with electronic signals to help us communicate or work
   Phones and computers are digital devices.

35. B — silver
   Silver is a colour.

36. C — A pen
   A pen gives clear permanent writing.

37. D — To stay safe
   Personal details should be protected.

38. B — To show who may speak
   Only the holder speaks.

39. C — It keeps order, peace and safety
   Obeying fair leaders keeps everyone safe.

40. B — Fair and kind
   The poem advises fairness and kindness.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Name then colon, capital letter to begin the words, end with a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark, a new line for each speaker.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: An advert aims to persuade people to buy, while news informs about events. An advert gives a price and where to buy, while news gives who, what, where and when.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for each difference.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read the title, read headings, read the first sentence of each paragraph, glance over the rest, say the main idea.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: A pace that is too fast makes words unclear, and one that is too slow loses interest. A good pace helps listeners follow and feel the mood.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of three ideas.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Simile: The teacher is as patient as a rock. Metaphor: The teacher is a walking dictionary.
   Working / marking points: One mark for a simile, one for a metaphor, one for clearly showing the difference.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put steps in order, begin each step with a verb, use short sentences, one action per step, add warnings.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Title, characters, setting, problem, events, ending (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each heading.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Neema: Wow! The sun is shining.
   Working / marking points: One mark for name with colon and one for an interjection.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: Title: How to keep our class clean. 1. Sweep the floor. 2. Wipe the desks. 3. Put waste in the bin. 4. Wash your hands. 5. Close the windows.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the title, one mark for each of four steps that begin with verbs and are in order.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Letters sit on the base line, tall letters reach the top line, keep a finger space between words, and start on the left.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule, up to three.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: Speak clearly, keep a steady pace, use a friendly and confident tone, pause at full stops and look at the audience.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct points.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: On Friday we bought rice, beans and flour.
   Working / marking points: One mark for capitals, one mark for the commas, one for the full stop.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Look at the whole picture, ask who where and what, plan the characters, setting, problem and ending, write the story in order, and check it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: close, sit
   Working / marking points: One mark for each verb.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Greet; say who you are and why you called; talk and listen; say goodbye. Example: Good afternoon, this is Neema speaking.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part and one mark for an example, with 4 marks maximum.

56. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four-line poem on the theme with a pair of rhyming lines, for example Feed the hen at break of day, Give her water, let her play, Kind hands keep her safe and well, That is how we care, we tell.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for theme, two marks for four lines and one mark for a rhyming pair.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read the title, read it aloud more than once, find meanings of new words, say the message in your own words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clear instructions tell people what to do to stay safe and dry, so they do not make mistakes or get hurt.
   Working / marking points: One mark for staying safe, one for avoiding mistakes, one for a clear link to rain.
